source_note: the reference shows no deer: it is only the dark pine forest edge whose palette and evening light the deer must match; draw one deer and nothing else, no trees, no figures
design: slender red deer doe with a warm russet-brown coat, a paler fawn belly, throat and inner legs, a cream rump patch and short white-edged tail, large dark eyes, big upright ears, a dark wet nose, thin legs with small dark hooves, no antlers
view_pose: Whole animal from the tips of its ears down to its hooves, standing square on all four hooves in a neutral alert pose, head level, short tail held down, nothing cropped; the spine points exactly along the view direction, so in a front or back view the body is foreshortened straight behind the head with the two front legs side by side and symmetric, not turned three-quarter, and in a profile view the spine runs exactly sideways
gait: Calm steady deer walk on the spot, one full stride a second: legs lifting high and delicately in turn, all four legs clearly alternating, back level, head held up and level, slight body bob; its body never moves forward
attack: lowers its head and neck down to graze the grass right at its front hooves, nibbling, then lifts its head back up to the start pose; all four hooves stay planted on the same spot
death: startles and drops: its legs fold under it and it sinks down onto its belly and then onto its side on the exact spot where it stood, head resting on the ground, legs stretched out; it never leaps or springs

view_notes.S: Seen exactly from the front, not three-quarter like a deer standing side-on: like looking at a deer walking straight at you, its head points straight at the camera with both of its eyes and both ears equally visible, and the face, neck and chest are square and symmetric about the image's vertical centre line. Only the front of the face, the throat and the chest show; the body is completely hidden straight behind the chest. The two front legs stand side by side, symmetric, and the two hind legs only just peek out behind them
